items.value: CORRECTION (load-bearing): the manifest declares worker as a POSITIONAL arg — `bp fleet beat <worker> [--status --ttl --agent --scope --capacity --dataset]`. The r2 task brief’s literal `--worker` example FAILS exit 2 ("unknown flag"), and under the brief’s own `|| true` swallow every beat would silently no-op forever: listeners beating into the void while green. Builders MUST use the positional form; run.go splitArgs rejects undeclared flags loudly (good — typos cannot vanish).
status=online/offline is REJECTED 422 by beat — self-declared vocab is idle|working|blocked only; offline is server-derived at read time. No harness/skill may ever beat status=online.

The wish (verbatim)

What we want is a simple system that makes the different dev servers be able to listnen and interact with orchestrator - the simplest and easiest the better - also we want a dev fleet system which is extendable - as said earlier - it is kinda personal + should be able to sync to many datasets and be some kinda main spot for developers to work. Ground truth at Strategize (2026-07-22, verified live)

• Round 1 MERGED: #5626 (sync-outbox listener exclusion, 060176daa) and #5627 (listener type + Barkpark.Tasks.Fleet zero-row beat + fail-closed roster + fleet.roster/fleet.beat manifest verbs, 57eaf52ec, merged 05:54Z). The PDF-D23 vocab review-fix rode #5627 before merge — no dangling -r branch.

Must re-probe at survey time; installed bp (built Jul 20) says 'unknown command fleet' — manifest-freshness or dynamic-dispatch question, the crux of wish item (1).
• Manifest contract on origin/main: fleet.beat takes worker as a POSITIONAL ARG, but the filed r2 task brief writes 'bp fleet beat --worker' — a real discrepancy the builder must resolve against bp fleet beat -h (the brief itself says to check).

The steward's reset is BARRED by the wish's own condition. Direction — close Wave A: the wave ends when the proof fires

The finished experience: a developer runs bp fleet roster on the binary they already have and sees a real table — every listener, online/offline computed server-side, current task joined. tooling/fleet/fleet-run.sh and both skills beat natively inside their single foreground loop; every 'until that ships' clause and the Herd contradiction are gone from the skills; a committed transcript proves the headline promise — kill a listener, the survivor stays ONLINE, the corpse flips OFFLINE exactly at its TTL and not before, with a negative control proving the check can fail. 1. CLI dialect = VERIFY-THEN-TRUST, zero-Go by default (PDF-D21). • WINNER — 'close the wave': all three wish items plus the safe half of the steward, with parallel r2∥r3 as the efficiency bold move. Sharpest attack #1: the scratch-target release may boot a CACHED build that predates #5627 — the harness would 404 on /v1/fleet/* and the proof dies confusingly, or worse a stale-green lies. Survey plan — 14 lanes, in flight

10. sync-guard-residue — any OTHER surface fanning or oddly rendering listener docs (webhooks, /v1/tasks/events, GitHub outbox, search, Studio browser). Why: cheap leak-catch.

DIGEST — what 14 survey lanes established

The direction survives intact and gets CHEAPER. The two absorbed attacks are both dead: guerrilla is fully live with round 1 (re-probed 2026-07-22 ~08:00Z — GET /v1/fleet/roster 200 {ok,documents}, POST beat zero-row registered:true/false, installed bp binary drives fleet roster/beat end-to-end, -o table renders a real 8-column table, and a probe listener flipped idle→offline past its TTL with no write), and manifest dispatch is genuinely zero-Go (no case "fleet" anywhere in cli.go; documents was already the first listEnvelopeKeys entry in internal/cli/table.go:69-73).
